title: Create your first workspace
summary: Set up a shared home for your team and your projects.
answer: A workspace brings your team, projects, and settings together. Start with one workspace, then invite the people who need access.

sections.title: Before you start
sections.html: Have a workspace name and your work email ready. If a teammate has already created a workspace, ask for an invitation to avoid creating a duplicate.

sections.title: Create the workspace
sections.html:
1. Sign in to your account.
  2. Choose Create workspace from the workspace menu.
  3. Enter a name your team will recognize.
  4. Review the settings, then select Create.

sections.title: Check that it worked
sections.html: Your new workspace appears in the workspace menu. Open it and check the name in the header. You can now invite a teammate or create your first project.

sections.title: If you cannot create a workspace
sections.html: Check whether your account has permission to create workspaces. If the option is missing, ask your administrator before creating another account.

title: Invite your team
summary: Bring the right people into your workspace.
answer: Workspace administrators can invite teammates by email and choose the level of access each person needs.

sections.title: Send an invitation
sections.html:
1. Open Settings → Members.
  2. Select Invite members.
  3. Enter the email address and choose a role.
  4. Review the invitation and select Send.

sections.title: Choose the right role
sections.html: Give each teammate only the access they need. Use an administrator role for people who manage the workspace and a member role for everyday work. Check your actual role permissions before inviting external collaborators.

sections.title: An invitation has not arrived
sections.html: Ask the recipient to check their spam folder and confirm the email address. Review the pending invitation before resending it.

title: Reset your password
summary: Get back into your account securely.
answer: Use the password reset option on the sign-in screen to request a reset link. If your account uses company single sign-on, reset your password with your identity provider instead.

sections.title: Request a reset link
sections.html:
1. Open the sign-in page.
  2. Select Forgot password?
  3. Enter the email you use for your account.
  4. Open the reset email and follow its instructions.
  5. Choose a new, unique password.

sections.title: The email has not arrived
sections.html: Check spam and confirm you entered the right address. Request a new link if the previous one has expired. Never share the reset link with anyone.

sections.title: Still locked out
sections.html: Contact your workspace administrator or the support team. Include your account email and the exact error message. Do not send your password.

title: Update your profile
summary: Keep your name and preferences up to date.
answer: You can change your display name and profile preferences from your account settings. Some details may be managed by your company.

sections.title: Edit your details
sections.html:
1. Open your profile menu.
  2. Select Account settings.
  3. Update your name and preferences.
  4. Select Save changes.

sections.title: Verify your changes
sections.html: Reload the page and check your profile menu. If an email change requires verification, complete that step before using the new address to sign in.

sections.title: Managed accounts
sections.html: If a field is locked, your company may manage it through single sign-on. Ask your administrator to update the source record.

title: Find and download invoices
summary: Find the billing documents your finance team needs.
answer: Workspace owners and billing administrators can find invoices in billing settings. If you do not see billing, ask the person who manages the subscription.

sections.title: Download an invoice
sections.html:
1. Open Settings → Billing.
  2. Find the invoice history.
  3. Choose the invoice for the correct billing period.
  4. Select Download and save a copy.

sections.title: An invoice is missing
sections.html: Check that you are in the correct workspace and using the billing account. If you still cannot find it, contact support with the billing period and workspace name.

sections.title: Billing details need changing
sections.html: Update the billing information for future invoices in billing settings. Ask support about corrections to an already issued invoice; do not edit the invoice yourself.

title: Change your subscription plan
summary: Review a plan change before you confirm it.
answer: Review features, limits, and the effective date in billing settings before changing your plan. Your product’s checkout should show the final cost and any proration.

sections.title: Review your options
sections.html:
1. Open Settings → Billing.
  2. Select Manage plan.
  3. Compare the available features and limits.
  4. Read the summary of charges and when the change takes effect.
  5. Confirm only after checking the impact on your workspace.

sections.title: Before a downgrade
sections.html: Check whether your workspace uses features or exceeds limits on the new plan. Export anything you need to keep and review the product’s retention policy.

sections.title: Check the result
sections.html: Return to billing settings to verify the plan and effective date. Save the confirmation for your records.

title: Organize your projects
summary: Make the next thing easy to find.
answer: Use consistent names and a small number of shared categories to help teammates find their work. Organize around the task people need to complete.

sections.title: Choose a naming pattern
sections.html: Use short, descriptive names such as “Customer onboarding” or “September launch.” Avoid names that only make sense to the person who created them.

sections.title: Create a project
sections.html:
1. Open your workspace.
  2. Select New project.
  3. Add a descriptive name and a short purpose.
  4. Assign an owner and confirm access.

sections.title: Keep it useful
sections.html: Archive completed projects after checking their retention requirements. Revisit the structure when people regularly ask where something belongs.

title: Manage team permissions
summary: Give people the access they need.
answer: Workspace administrators should review permissions when someone joins, changes role, or leaves. Give the smallest level of access that supports their work.

sections.title: Review a member
sections.html:
1. Open Settings → Members.
  2. Select the person you want to review.
  3. Check their current role and access.
  4. Choose the appropriate role and save.

sections.title: Before removing access
sections.html: Transfer ownership of active work and verify that another administrator can manage the workspace. Follow your organization’s offboarding policy.

sections.title: Confirm the change
sections.html: Check the member list after saving. Where possible, use a test account to verify what each role can see.

title: Connect an integration
answer: An administrator can connect supported tools from the integrations settings. Review the permissions requested by each integration before authorizing access.

sections.title: Connect the tool
sections.html:
1. Open Settings → Integrations.
  2. Choose a supported integration.
  3. Select Connect.
  4. Sign in to the external tool and review the requested permissions.
  5. Authorize the connection and run a small test.

sections.title: Verify the connection
sections.html: Check that the integration reports a connected state, then confirm the expected action in the external tool. Start with test data that does not contain sensitive information.

sections.title: Disconnect a tool
sections.html: Use the integration settings to disconnect access. Review the external tool’s authorized applications as well, and remove any credentials you no longer use.

title: An integration is not syncing
answer: Check the connection status, permissions, and recent errors first. Reconnecting immediately can hide useful error details or create duplicate data.

sections.title: Check the basics
sections.html:
1. Confirm the integration is enabled.
  2. Check the account that authorized it still has access.
  3. Review the last successful sync and any error messages.
  4. Check the external provider’s service status.

sections.title: Try a small test
sections.html: Create one harmless test item and check whether it arrives. Record the time and the item identifier so support can trace it.

sections.title: Ask for help
sections.html: Share the integration name, the time of the last successful sync, and a redacted error message. Never include API keys or authorization tokens.

title: I cannot sign in
summary: Work through the most common sign-in issues.
answer: Confirm your email address and sign-in method first. If your company uses single sign-on, use the company sign-in option rather than a password reset.

sections.title: Check your sign-in method
sections.html: Use the method you originally registered with. A password, Google sign-in, and company SSO may follow different account recovery flows.

sections.title: Try these checks
sections.html:
1. Check your email address for a typo.
  2. Open a new private browser window.
  3. If you use a password, request a reset.
  4. If you use SSO, ask your administrator to confirm your access.

sections.title: Contact support
sections.html: Include the exact error message, your browser, and the time the problem happened. Do not share your password, reset link, or two-factor authentication codes.

title: Report a problem
summary: Give support the details that help them help you.
answer: A useful problem report explains what you tried, what you expected, and what happened instead. Include the smallest set of steps that reproduces the issue.

sections.title: Collect these details
sections.html:
• The page or feature affected.
  • The steps you took.
  • What you expected and what actually happened.
  • The exact error and when you saw it.
  • Your browser and device.

sections.title: Protect sensitive information
sections.html: Remove customer data, payment details, passwords, and API keys from screenshots and logs. Share only what support needs to understand the issue.

sections.title: Send your report
sections.html: Use the contact route your team has published. Keep replies in the same conversation so the history stays together.
